unit.title: Latinisms & Learned Expressions
unit.subtitle: A priori, grosso modo, motu proprio and the traps around them

grammar.title: The Latin that educated Spanish still speaks
grammar.intro: Formal and written Spanish is threaded with untranslated latinismos — a priori, grosso modo, statu quo, motu proprio. Used well they sound precise and cultured; used wrong they instantly betray you. The traps are almost always the same: an intruding preposition (a grosso modo ✗) or a mangled vowel (de motu propio ✗). This unit fixes the form and the meaning of each.

sections.heading: Reasoning: a priori, a posteriori, per se, ipso facto
sections.body: A priori means “beforehand, without checking the facts”; a posteriori, “after the fact, from experience”. Per se means “in itself, by its very nature”. Ipso facto means “immediately, right then and there”. These carry no extra preposition beyond the ones shown.
conj: beforehand / on the face of it

ex.es: A priori, la idea parece sensata, pero habría que probarla.
ex.en: On the face of it, the idea seems sensible, but it would need testing.

ex.es: El dinero no da la felicidad per se.
ex.en: Money doesn't bring happiness in itself.

sections.heading: Manner and place: grosso modo, in situ, motu proprio
sections.body: Grosso modo means “roughly, broadly speaking” — and takes no “a” before it. In situ means “on site, in the original place”. Motu proprio means “of one's own accord”; the second word is proprio (with the extra r) and it is never preceded by “de”.
conj: of one's own accord (NOT 'de motu propio')

ex.es: Grosso modo, el proyecto costará unos dos millones.
ex.en: Roughly speaking, the project will cost about two million.

ex.es: Se disculpó motu proprio, sin que nadie se lo pidiera.
ex.en: He apologised of his own accord, without anyone asking.

sections.heading: States and conditions: statu quo, de facto, sine qua non
sections.body: Statu quo (the current state of affairs) is written statu, not “status”, in this fixed phrase. De facto means “in practice, whether official or not”, opposed to de iure/de jure (“by law”). A condición sine qua non is an absolutely essential requirement — one without which nothing else holds.

ex.es: Nadie quiere alterar el statu quo antes de las elecciones.
ex.en: Nobody wants to disturb the status quo before the elections.

ex.es: La confianza es una condición sine qua non del acuerdo.
ex.en: Trust is a sine qua non for the agreement.

sections.heading: Handy extras: alter ego, modus operandi, in extremis, viceversa
sections.body: Alter ego is a second self or trusted stand-in. Modus operandi is a characteristic way of doing things. In extremis means “at the last moment / in a desperate situation”. Viceversa means “the other way round” and, unlike the others, is written as one fully Spanish word.

ex.es: El detective reconoció enseguida su modus operandi.
ex.en: The detective recognised his modus operandi at once.

ex.es: Aprobó el examen in extremis, con el tiempo justo.
ex.en: She passed the exam at the very last minute, with no time to spare.

takeaways: grosso modo and motu proprio take NO preposition: never 'a grosso modo', never 'de motu propio'.
It is motu proprio (with the r), not 'motu propio'.
In the fixed phrase it's statu quo, not 'status quo'.
per se = in itself; a priori = beforehand; a posteriori = after the fact; ipso facto = immediately.

mistakes.w: A grosso modo, serán unos cien.
mistakes.why: Grosso modo never takes 'a' — the Latin ablative already carries the meaning.
No 'de', and the correct form is 'proprio' (with the extra r), not 'propio'.

mistakes.w: No hay que cambiar el status quo.
mistakes.r: No hay que cambiar el statu quo.
mistakes.why: In this Latin phrase the word is 'statu' (ablative), not the English 'status'.

exercises.prompt: ___, el plan parece viable, aunque aún no lo hemos analizado a fondo.
exercises.prompt_en: On the face of it, the plan seems viable, though we haven't analysed it in depth yet.
exercises.ok: ¡Correcto! Un juicio previo a los datos → a priori.
exercises.no: A judgment made before examining the evidence is “a priori”.

exercises.prompt: Elige la forma correcta: “Lo calculé ___, sin entrar en detalles.”
exercises.prompt_en: Choose the correct form: “I estimated it roughly, without going into detail.”
exercises.no: It's simply “grosso modo”, with no preposition — never 'a grosso modo'.

exercises.prompt: Build: "He resigned of his own accord."
exercises.ok: ¡Perfecto! motu proprio, sin 'de' y con la r.
exercises.no: It's “motu proprio” — no 'de', and 'proprio' with the extra r.

exercises.prompt: La honestidad es una condición ___ para cualquier pacto duradero.
exercises.prompt_en: Honesty is a sine qua non for any lasting agreement.
exercises.hint: Latin for an absolutely indispensable condition.
exercises.no: An indispensable requirement is a condición “sine qua non”.

exercises.prompt: Match each Latinism to its meaning.

exercises.tts: Nadie quería alterar el statu quo antes de las elecciones.
accepted: nadie queria alterar el statu quo antes de las elecciones
exercises.translation: Nobody wanted to disturb the status quo before the elections.
exercises.no: It was: “Nadie quería alterar el statu quo antes de las elecciones.” (statu, not status).

exercises.scenario: A junior colleague proofreads your report and hesitates over a phrase ✍️

lines.speaker: Dani
lines.es: Aquí has puesto “se disculpó motu proprio”. ¿No sería “de motu propio”?
lines.en: Here you wrote “se disculpó motu proprio”. Shouldn't it be “de motu propio”?

options.text: No, es “motu proprio”: sin “de” y con la segunda r. “De motu propio” es un error muy extendido.
Tienes razón, lo correcto es “de motu propio”; lo cambio ahora mismo.
Da igual, las dos formas se aceptan por igual en un texto formal.

exercises.ok: ¡Perfecto! motu proprio, sin 'de' y con la r doble.
exercises.no: The correct form is “motu proprio” (no 'de', with the extra r) — option a corrects it.

exercises.say: Grosso modo, el dinero no da la felicidad per se.
exercises.en: Roughly speaking, money doesn't bring happiness in itself.
exercises.no: Almost — tap “Hear it”, then match the rhythm of “Grosso modo, el dinero no da la felicidad per se.”

vocab.en: beforehand, on the face of it
